prompt.content:
You are analyzing the evaluation of one candidate change to a 3D-IC physical design flow.
Hypothesis of the change: Recent gate failures suggest the parent patch's `_macro_criticality` attribute path is fragile; make the criticality-aware repair robust by falling back to a degree-based proxy when criticality is unavailable, and modestly reduce the shrink coefficient (3.0 -> 2.0) to fine-tune the best candidate while keeping the criticality-weighted contrastive loss.
Rule-based digest:
total=-inf robust(mean-std)=-inf min_case=-inf all_valid=False
  failures: bp_fe-ng45/1001:stage timeout; bp_fe-ng45/1002:HBT min-spacing violation; bp_fe-ng45/1003:HBT min-spacing violation; bp-ng45/1001:stage timeout; bp-ng45/1002:stage timeout; bp-ng45/1003:legalization overlap
Write <=120 words. If some runs are INVALID (failures listed), first say what kind of failure it is (legality / crash / timeout) and whether it looks systematic (all seeds of a case) or sporadic - an invalid candidate says nothing about the hypothesis itself; suggest how to make the same idea legal. Otherwise: (1) did the hypothesis hold? (2) which case/metric moved and plausible mechanism, (3) one concrete next-step suggestion. No preamble.

response: Invalid: mixed legality (HBT min-spacing, legalization overlap) and stage timeouts, systematic across all seeds of both bp_fe-ng45 and bp-ng45 cases—so this candidate says nothing about the hypothesis. The degree-based fallback and shrink change can't be assessed. To make the idea legal: gate the fallback behind an explicit criticality-availability check with logging, and validate the 2.0 shrink on a single case first to rule out spacing/overlap regressions before full sweeps; also add per-stage timeouts to distinguish timeout from legality.
